exposure: type of community maternity caregiver (private obstetrician, GP, midwife)
intended mode of birth (planned caesarean, intended vaginal birth)
cohort: The study included 248,424 singleton pregnancies under private obstetrician and community maternity care with a live birth in New Zealand between January 2016 and June 2020.
finding: Adjusted mean healthcare costs were significantly higher for private obstetricians compared to community maternity caregivers (mostly midwives) and for elective caesarean section compared to intended vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean section was found to be more costly than intended vaginal birth by $4,316.
